newsitem.title: USA: MaxServ still willing to talk with Sears.
newsitem.headline: MaxServ still willing to talk with Sears.

text.p: MaxServ Inc said on Wednesday that, while a special committee of its board rejected a $7 per share takeover bid from Sears, it remained willing to negotiate a transaction at a mutually acceptable price.
The company said it rejected the bid as "inadequate" after deliberations with its financial advisor, Broadview Associates and its legal counsel.
Sears said Tuesday it withdrew its bid for the outstanding shares of MaxServ.

"Based on preliminary inquires received by Broadview, the special committee believes that the sale of 100 percent of MaxServ to a third party in a transaction voluntarily supported by Sears might command a significantly higher valuation," the company said.

MaxServ said the committee was intent on working with Sears to maximize MaxServ's shareholders' value either as an independent public compan in an acquisition or in an acquisition by a third party with Sears' support.

Prior to the filing of the amended Schedule 13D, Sears was advised that a proposal in the range of $8 to $10 per share would be supported by the special committee, MaxServ said. After Sears' recent filing, the committee narrowed its range of acceptable values to between $8 and $9 per share, it said.
